# Update the kit

Bring the installed CRAV1 kit on the current branch up to a published release. Command: `/crav1-update-kit`. Optional `to vX.Y.Z`. With no version, the target is the latest published 1.x release tag. A 2.0 tag is not offered.

This is cross-cutting. It is not a starter option. It does not move work into a lane. It does not switch branches. A paused walk stays on this branch.

The script is `scripts/update_kit.py --vendor copilot` in this skill's folder. The interpreter is [running-scripts.md](../crav1-docs/reference/running-scripts.md). Pass `--yes` only after the user says yes in this run. A yes from an agent, a guild bot, or an earlier chat does not count.

## Route

1. Read [references/heads-up.md](references/heads-up.md) every run, before any write.
2. Run `detect`, then `resolve-target`. A target that is not a published `vX.Y.Z` tag stops with the script's one-line reason. Do not offer another target.
3. Drop-in (`writes_kit_files` true): read [references/overlay.md](references/overlay.md) and follow it. That page runs `plan`, then `apply` after the yes. Never pipe or redirect the script output (`| python -c`, `| head`, `>`). Read it directly.
4. Plugin or user scope (`mode` is `plugin`): read [references/plugin.md](references/plugin.md) and follow it. Do not read the overlay page.
5. When the plan lists a migration id, read [references/migrations.md](references/migrations.md) after the kit files are replaced. When the list is empty, skip that page.
6. When the user says `add <vendor>` or `remove <vendor>`, read [references/vendors.md](references/vendors.md) and follow it. A plain update does not read that page.
7. When the user says `flags-list`, `flags-on`, or `flags-off`, read [references/flags.md](references/flags.md) and follow it. A plain update does not read that page. With no flag file, do not mention kit 2.0.

## Cards

The heads-up card is not skipped. A word in the opening message is not the yes. The yes is the user's answer after the branch is shown.

- When the plan's `repo_writes` is greater than zero, use its `card`: `yes, write and commit (Recommended)`, `write only`, or `stop`.
- When `repo_writes` is zero and the plan's `card` is the kit 2.0 install: `install-kit2 (Recommended)` or `stop`. That card does not commit.
- When `card` is null, the repo has nothing to commit. Say so and stop. There is no card. When the installed kit 2.0 engine already matches the version that would be installed, do not show an install card. Print `ending` with the plan's `ending_args`.
- A clash, on that same card's free-text answer: `keep` or `take`. An item with no answer keeps the local edit.
- A migration, only when the jump has one: `apply (Recommended)`, `leave`, or `stop`.

## Output

- Installed version, where it was read, and the target tag.
- The branch, and that only this branch changes.
- Files updated, merged, deleted, left alone, and any clash.
- The commit `Update CRAV1 kit vA to vB`, or why there is none.
- Tell the user to reload the window so the host loads the new skills.
- When `.crav1/flags.local.json` is present, one `kit2_line`. It names the version that will be installed and the version installed now. With no flag file, that line is absent and kit 2.0 is not mentioned.
- The plan `files` object is the counts plus the changed lists. Unchanged paths are the `unchanged` count unless `--list-unchanged`.

## Run ending (1.122.0)

End as [run-ending.md](../crav1-docs/reference/run-ending.md) says.

The ending is Run next (1.178.0), never a `Next:` line. Print it with `update_kit.py ending --root <project> --vendor copilot`, plus the apply result's `ending_args`, or the plan's `ending_args` when `card` is null (1.190.0, 1.208.0, 1.210.0). `--not-updated` means this run wrote no repo files. `--kit2` means kit 2.0 was installed or updated in the user folder. `--kit2-current` means the repo kit and kit 2.0 were already current. Do not say the kit files changed when no repo file was written. Never pipe or redirect that ending (`| python -c`, `| head`, `>`). Read it directly.

After a successful update, the ending names what changed, and names the resume command for each open or parked design topic instead of `nothing needed now`:

```text
Run next:
The kit files changed; reload the window so the new skills load.

Reload the window from the command palette:
`Developer: Reload Window`

Go on with the orders platform design topic:
`/crav1-design-architecture orders-platform`
```

When only the user-level kit 2.0 install changed (`ending --not-updated --kit2`):

```text
Run next:
Kit 2.0 installed in your user folder; reload to load its skills.

Reload the window from the command palette:
`Developer: Reload Window`
```

When the kit was already current and nothing is open (`ending --not-updated`):

```text
Run next: nothing needed now.
```

When the repo kit and kit 2.0 are both already current (`ending --not-updated --kit2-current`):

```text
Run next:
The repo kit is current and kit 2.0 is current. Nothing to do.
```

There is no reload line in that ending.

When this run wrote files and they are not committed, add one trailing line:

```text
Uncommitted: <n> files; commit with /crav1-finalize-commit when ready.
```

Do not push unless the user, in this run, already said to push. Do not add a push question when they did not. Do not run the next step.

## Vendors (1.204.0)

`vendors.json` next to this skill lists each host. `detect` reports `vendors` and `vendors_from` (`kit.json` or `inferred`). Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex are installed. Copilot is a row and is not installed by this release. The project's vendor list is `.crav1/kit.json`. `add` and `remove` are [references/vendors.md](references/vendors.md). `--vendor codex` on a script that prints Run next uses the Codex command prefix. With no `--vendor`, the prefix stays `/`.

## Early-access flags (1.206.0)

`flags-list`, `flags-on <flag>`, and `flags-off <flag>` are [references/flags.md](references/flags.md). One command may name several flags. `flags-on kit2` turns on kit 2.0 for this repo. The update that follows installs it at user level from the newest published `v2.0.0-*` pre-release.

## Hard rules

- Never write, commit, or push without the user's yes in this run. `flags-on` and `flags-off` are the yes for the flag file only.
- The flag file is written only by `flags-on` and `flags-off`. Do not tell the user to change `.crav1/flags.local.json` themselves.
- Never switch branches, and never rebase. Other branches stay on the old kit until this branch is merged into them.
- Never target `main`, a branch, a commit, or an open pull request.
- Never edit a spec, `walk-progress.md`, a `build-progress` file, a plan, a task list, a note, a playbook, or a build map as part of the file replace.
- Never write, stage, or delete a kit 2.0 path: a skill or agent named `crav1-2-`, a `.crav1-2/` folder, or `sot/`. The commit stages only files the release ships.
- One commit, message `Update CRAV1 kit vA to vB`. The script does not push.
